I can actually see how The Chairman could be easier in battle than Voss if Legacy is invovled, since he can become immune to a type of damage, and with The Chairman's deck it is solely Projectile and Melee damage. With Legacy Leading from the Front and with his Next Evolution he can easily stomp on The Chairman fairly easily. Now throw in Tempest and Ra, like this topic is originally about, if they get all their correct cards out as well it is a unstoppable force to be reckoned with.

 

As for Voss, his minions do various types of damages, one of which is immune to fire which could spell for a wasted turn if Ra has Imbue Fire and is the last in the turn order. Then of course Forced Deployment will be the main concern. Unless, you've got Tempest buffed up with some Galvanize and Inspiring Presence, which would allow his Innate power to clear the field (besides ones who are immune to projectile), but even just Galvanize would lead to wiping out the field if Tempest already has Grevious Hailstorm.

 

But anyways, just a quick question for Legacy, do you play every game with Legacy, Tempest, and Ra, or do you play a variety of combinations? I ask because I am curious as to how important winning is to you. (No rudeness intended if it comes off that way.)

pcgamerpirate wrote:
So you whittled down his deck so fast that the operative wasn't able to do that much damage for destroying villain cards?We always put Fanatic on Zealous offense duty when it comes to the chairman.  
And as of EE I don't even think that works. Zealous Offense no longer affects character cards at all, correct? 
 
Darken the Skies and Prison Break can both serve that role, respectively. Not generally as backbreaking as Forced Deployment at the right (wrong) time, but still pretty disheartening.

Zealous Offence doesn't work against the Operative, but it does work against Hired Guns, The Muscle and Enforcers, and it's probably better to leave those guys out unable to inflict damage than to kill them and let them come back again and hit with full force. I disagree about Forced Deployment being worse than Prison Break. As far as I'm concerned, the order is Prison Break > Forced Deployment > Darken the Skies. Especially on Advanced Mode, getting even one Hired Gun out while the Chairman is flipped is a world of pain.
